question.text: As a result of his victory at Hastings, this Norman was crowned King of England. He later commissioned the Domesday Book.
question.answerHtml: William the Conqueror [or William I; or William, Duke of Normandy; or William the Bastard; prompt on “William” alone]
question.clue: This king ordered for a destructive campaign to gain control of Northumbria in his Harrying of the North, and he ordered for the compilation of a written record of England, the Domesday Book.

swap.text: In response to the famine, the UK repealed these laws, which imposed tariffs on imported grains, not a vegetable with yellow kernels as the name would suggest.
swap.clue: These laws were introduced during the Premiership of Lord Liverpool, and were supported by economist Thomas Malthus.

question.leadin: This leader crushed the Scots in the Battle of Worcester, a victory which caused Charles II to flee to France.
question.text: Name this Lord Protector of the England, who participated in the English Civil War.
question.clue: The historian John Morrill called this man a "proto-fascist" for his actions at Drogheda and Wexford, after which 50,000 Irish people were deported.

swap.leadin: Name some dudes who were decapitated.
swap.text: This King of England is said to have worn two shirts to his execution, to prevent from shivering in the cold and appearing afraid. He was killed during the English Civil War.
swap.clue: This ruler was depicted "at the hunt" by his court painter, Anthony van Dyck.

question.leadin: This country is one of the few that still has a Historiographer Royal.
question.text: Name this European country, whose Neolithic archaeological sites include Skara Brae ("SKAR-ah BRAY") on the Orkney Islands.
question.clue: Peter and Eileen Caddy founded the New Age Findhorn Community in this country.

swap.leadin: William Thomas Turner was the captain of this ship, and is sometimes blamed for his failure to adopt the evasive zig-zag course.
swap.text: Name this British passenger ship, the sinking of which prompted U.S. entry into World War One.
swap.clue: Travelers on this ship were warned that a "state of war exists" by a newspaper ad plaed by the Imperial German Embassy.

question.leadin: This man banished all Jews from England in the 1290 Edict of Expulsion.
question.text: Name this English king, whose nickname refers to his above average height. Before he acceded to the throne, he defeated an alliance of barons who revolted against his father, Henry III.
question.clue: This ruler led a force which defeated William Wallace at the Battle of Falkirk, despite previously losing at Stirling Bridge.

swap.leadin: FTPE, name some modern British capital-C Conservatives.
swap.text: This Epping M.P. succeeded Neville Chamberlain and, offering nothing but "blood, toil, tears, and sweat," led the British to victory in the Second World War.
swap.clue: Clement Attlee replaced this man at the Potsdam Conference after the Conservatives were voted out in July 1945.

question.leadin: Appointed junior lord of the Treasury by Robert Peel, he was responsible for the 1844 Railway Bill.
question.text: Name this frequent Liberal prime minister and rival of Benjamin Disraeli.
question.clue: This politician's pamphlet Bulgarian Horrors criticized both the Ottoman reprisal against the title minority and Benjamin Disraeli's government indifference to the matter.

swap.leadin: Lord Sidmouth's repressive Six Acts were passed in the aftermath of this event.
swap.text: Name this event in which William Hulton's 15th Hussars cavalry charged upon a crowd of reformers in Manchester.
swap.clue: The Earl of Liverpool's government responded to it by passing the repressive Six Acts.

question.text: The translations carried out by Alfred and his scholars mostly rendered Latin texts in this Anglo-Saxon language used to write Beowulf.
question.answerHtml: Old English [do not accept or prompt on “English” or “Middle English”]

swap.text: In order to honor Albert, Victoria wore her wedding dress at one of these events in 1897, becoming the first British monarch to be given one. The second of these events to occur took place for Queen Elizabeth II in 2012.
swap.clue: The prime ministers of eleven colonies gathered at St. Paul's Cathedral to celebrate this event in 1897.

question.text: This British general was the victor at Omdurman. He later became Secretary of State for War, and a popular WWI poster displayed his face above the caption "wants you!"
question.clue: Eventually killed by a German mine while on board the Hampshire, his mustachioed countenance adorned many a British World War I recruiting poster, part of his successful effort to recruit volunteers as Secretary of State for War.

swap.text: Tony Judt's Postwar notes that the "decline of the moral authority of the British establishment" began with the trial, and continued with this party's legalization of abortion under Home Secretary Roy Jenkins. This party lost the 1979 general election to the Conservatives.
swap.clue: Ramsay MacDonald was the first prime minister from this party, while another won largely by campaigning on the idea of a "New" version of it.

question.leadin: This person's army defeated that of Ralph the Timid, and then sacked the city of Hereford.
question.text: Name this person, who conquered Deheubarth in 1055 to become the only native Welsh ruler to unite all of Wales, and as such is regarded as the only King of Wales.
question.answerHtml: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn [‘Griffith’ ap ‘Clew-well-in’; prompt on partial answer]

swap.leadin: It was originally organized as the anti-federalist party, and the whip of this party was withdrawn from Godfrey Bloom after he attacked a journalist in the street.
swap.text: Name this far-right political party in the UK led by Nigel Farange.

question.text: Among the founding members of the company was Sebastian, an explorer with this surname. Sebastian's father, who also held this surname, led a British expedition to the coast of North America in 1497.
question.clue: That explorer believed he had reached Asia after discovering Cape North, St. Paul Island, and Miquelon in his ship the Matthew.

swap.leadin: Name these politicians of the World War I era.
swap.text: This British foreign secretary failed to preserve the peace, and his reluctance to commit Britain to war with Germany might have encouraged German aggression. He is known for remarking "The lamps are going out all over Europe; we shall not see them lit again in our lifetime."

question.leadin: Answer the following about the 1970-1974 premiership of Ted Heath.
question.text: In 1974, Heath disastrously introduced this energy-saving measure during a crippling coal miners' strike. This policy permitted the use of electricity only during a specified period of time.

swap.leadin: Identify the following relating to the problem of longitude, FTPE.
swap.text: Thanks to the influence of King George III, this self-taught British clockmaker finally was awarded the complete twenty thousand pound longitude prize for his H-4 chronometer in 1773.
